title: Procedural shapes and mesh generators
summary: Generate mathematical surfaces and procedural meshes, then inspect how their parameters change the geometry.

blocks.text: retiam/shapes supplies option-driven paths for stars, squircles, hearts, crosses, gears, teardrops, chevrons, curved/double arrows, architectural profiles, spirals, waveforms, diamonds, trapezoids, parallelograms and crescents. It also exposes additional arc, annulus, regular-polygon, sector and wedge helpers. These inherit Path behavior, so effects, modifiers, transforms and sampling remain available.
The current index contains more shapes than older “16 shapes” catalog counts imply. The shapes API lists every exported class and options interface; use that as the inventory.

Capsule, rounded box, prism, pyramid, Platonic solids, torus knot, helix, tube, ellipsoid, gear, truncated cone, wedge, diamond, bipyramid and superellipsoid generators create Model-compatible meshes. Radius, segment counts, topology, caps and profile parameters are shape-specific; do not assume all constructors accept the same positional arguments.

A smooth mesh needs coherent normals and consistent winding. Flat-shaded solids require face-specific vertices/normals at sharp edges. Tubes use a transported frame along their centerline so the cross-section does not twist arbitrarily at each sample. Closed paths require a seam treatment; tight bends can produce overlapping tube geometry. Increase sampling until visible curvature is stable, then profile its memory and shading cost.
Study one parameterized 2D contour and one parameterized 3D mesh separately.
